steps.title: What is a wallet?
steps.body: A wallet doesn't hold coins. It holds the keys that prove an account on the blockchain is yours.

steps.title: Public and private keys
steps.body: Your public key is your address: share it with anyone. Your private key signs your actions. Whoever has it controls the account.

steps.title: Test SOL on Devnet
steps.body: Devnet is Solana's test network. SOL here has no real value, and you can get it for free from the faucet.

steps.title: Why do you need SOL?
steps.body: Creating an account takes up space on the blockchain, and that space is paid for in SOL. So creating your profile proves you have SOL and know how to sign.

quiz.question: Which one should you never share?
quiz.explanation: Your private key signs for you. Whoever has it can move everything you own.

quiz.question: Does Devnet SOL have real value?
quiz.explanation: It's a test network: SOL is free and meant for experimenting.

task.title: Create your on-chain profile
task.description: This creates your player account. It stores your level, points and items, and pays a small rent in SOL.

steps.title: What is a transaction?
steps.body: A signed request to change the state of the blockchain: move SOL, create an account or call a program.

steps.title: Signatures
steps.body: Your wallet signs with your private key. The network checks that the signature matches your address without ever seeing the key.

steps.title: Fees and lamports
steps.body: Every transaction pays a small fee. A lamport is the smallest unit of SOL.

steps.title: The Explorer
steps.body: Every transaction has a unique signature. On Solana Explorer, anyone can see what happened.

quiz.question: How many lamports are in 1 SOL?
quiz.explanation: One billion. That's why fees look like big numbers in lamports.

quiz.question: Who signs your transactions?
quiz.explanation: Only your wallet holds the private key. No app signs for you.

task.title: Send 0.01 SOL
task.description: The transfer is made by the program instruction that completes the level. Pick an address that isn't yours.

steps.title: Everything is an account
steps.body: On Solana, data lives in accounts. Your balance, your profile and programs themselves are all accounts.

steps.title: Programs
steps.body: A program is code deployed on the blockchain. It doesn't store data itself: it reads and writes other accounts.

steps.title: Rent
steps.body: Every account must hold enough SOL for the space it uses. Closing the account gives that SOL back.

steps.title: PDAs
steps.body: A PDA is an address derived from a program and some seeds. It has no private key: only the program can sign for it.

quiz.question: Who can sign for a PDA?
quiz.explanation: A PDA has no private key. Only its program can sign for it.

quiz.question: What does rent pay for?
quiz.explanation: The more data an account stores, the more SOL it must hold.

task.title: Create an on-chain note
task.description: Your note will live in a PDA derived from your wallet. Write anything you like, up to 100 characters.
